gaps.sentence: 'The road is being resurfaced,' the council said. The council said the road ___ resurfaced.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive (is being resurfaced) backshifts to past continuous passive: was being resurfaced.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll finish the report today,' she said. She said she would finish the report ___.
gaps.explanation: Today becomes that day when reported later.

gaps.sentence: They ___ us that the museum had closed early.
gaps.explanation: Tell somebody (that)... — 'told' needs the direct personal object 'us'; 'said' cannot take it.

gaps.sentence: 'Please, please don't leave me,' he sobbed. He begged her ___ leave him.
gaps.hint: beg sb not to do sth
gaps.explanation: Negative begging: begged her not to leave; the negative precedes the infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
'Do you take sugar?' he asked. He asked ___ took sugar.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no questions take if/whether, not do-support or 'that': asked if I took sugar.

gaps.sentence: 'You broke my phone!' she said to her brother. She ___ her brother of breaking her phone.
'Watch out for the ice on the road,' she said. She ___ us about the icy road.
gaps.explanation: Warnings about a danger: warn somebody about something (or warn sb to do).
